description: Every Minecraft world-seed range that a live run, plan or experiment declaration of this project used or reserved. tests/test_seed_registry.py expands every plan and declaration under configs/ (subfolders included) and every retained results/**/metadata.json. It fails on a used seed that no range of its experiment covers; on a seed that several experiments use when the one range holding it does not name them all; on a held-out range used by more than one experiment; on any training run on a held-out range; on any evaluation on a training range; and on a committed plan outside configs/. A second test pass inside one experiment is not detected here: the experiment's declaration governs it (docs/stone_tools_design.md section 8.5). A declaration's world seeds are read from any key ending in world_seeds ([first, last] or 'first-last'), from world_seeds_from or first_world_seed with an episodes or episodes_per_policy count beside it, and from resource-train and resource-demo commands that state --world-seed; any other key naming a seed fails unless it is agent_seed, agent_seeds, seed_note, seed_notes or a seed inside an agent or learner block. Every such field counts as the declaring experiment's own use, so the seeds of another experiment's checkpoint (for example the stage-1 policy) are written as prose, such as 'trained on worlds 100-149 at 87673b8', which is only checked to be registered. Before committing a new plan or declaration, add its own path to its experiment's sources and register its seeds here; before retaining runs, add the retained folder itself to its experiment's sources, never a folder above it, because the longest source path decides the owner.
seed_rule: A run started with --world-seed f and --episodes n plays world seeds f to f + n - 1, episode k on f + k - 1 (infrastructure/resource_session.py); --world-seed defaults to 42 (infrastructure/__main__.py). A scheduler job uses first_world_seed and episodes the same way. An evaluation job with c chunks plays consecutive blocks of that range, the first n mod c chunks one episode longer, chunk k with agent seed agent_seed + k - 1 (infrastructure/parallel_runs.py, parse_plan). A continuation folder -partN starts at f plus the episodes already attempted, with the rest of the count, so it stays inside f to f + n - 1. A retained run counts first_world_seed to first_world_seed + episodes_requested - 1 from its metadata.json as used, whether or not every episode was played.

kinds.development: Worlds for building and debugging helpers; reusable; never validation or test evidence
kinds.validation: Worlds declared in advance to check helpers or choose settings; may inform fixes; never a held-out test
kinds.training: Worlds on which live learners update their tables
kinds.test: Held-out worlds for one experiment's frozen policies; never used before it and never used to choose anything
kinds.replacement test: A held-out range kept unused, for testing again if the code changes after the first test episode
kinds.benchmark: Worlds of an engineering check that says nothing about learning
kinds.example: Seeds printed in an example file; reserved so that no experiment copies them
kinds.filler: Worlds that only keep a parallel slot busy; never analysed or reported
